title: Your Frying Pan Helped Build the Atomic Bomb
alt_titles: The Accident Inside Every Non-Stick Pan
A Gas Vanished in 1938. It Became Teflon.
description:
On 6 April 1938, a 27-year-old DuPont chemist named Roy Plunkett opened a cylinder of gas and nothing came out. The cylinder was still heavy. When he cut it open, he found a white, waxy powder that nothing would stick to and almost nothing could destroy. He had made polytetrafluoroethylene, PTFE, by accident.

For years nobody knew what to do with it. Then the Manhattan Project needed a material that could survive uranium hexafluoride, one of the most corrosive substances ever handled in industry. PTFE coated the valves and seals of the enrichment plant at Oak Ridge. After the war it got a brand name, Teflon, and a French engineer and his wife put it on a frying pan.

This is the story of the slipperiest material on Earth: the accident, the bomb, the kitchen, and the hidden flaw that took decades to come out.
